sourceClaims.label: The review covers update.ts and its paired update.test.ts suite.
The suite uses hermetic temporary roots and restores process state.
Results and reason arrays receive exact whole-value and ordering assertions.
Git and filesystem boundaries use fakes or local temporary directories without network access.
Negative controls and multi-element cases provide strong positive coverage.
The dropCache failure case does not discriminate removal of the drop call.
Abort cleanup cases do not directly observe cleanup effects.
Warm-cache SHA proof asserts clone count but not the complete Git call sequence.
Many tests omit Arrange-Act-Assert comments.
makeCtx uses double casts to satisfy broad interfaces.
Production catch blocks cast unknown values directly to Error.
updateSinglePlugin reads process.cwd directly.
Production update logic constructs Date values inline.
UpdatePluginsOptions lacks top-level documentation.
The production and paired test modules are oversized.
The module should be split along preflight, swap, and cascade boundaries.
The default cascade dependency remains a hard-coded integration seam.
Current whole-message sibling tests demonstrate the preferred assertion pattern.
Messaging-row and support modules are outside this review's scope.
The historical review did not run tests or coverage.
The review covers plan, apply, and apply-outcomes production-test pairs.
Tests use fresh literals and exact whole-value expectations.
Planner tests prove complete plans, purity, determinism, and enabled-state distinctions.
Apply tests exercise real orchestrators by design and discriminate their behavior.
Notification-boundary tests use a strong hermetic recording double.
Apply-outcomes tests cover clean and hybrid outcomes.
Several tests use a generic result variable name.
No focused case isolates a config-to-record mismatch without an artifact diff.
diffMarketplaces has no explicit default branch for future variants.
applySourceMismatches has no explicit default branch for future causes.
Apply hard-codes five orchestrator dependencies through static imports.
The static imports prevent lightweight behavior doubles.
classifyOrchestratorThrow has no explicit default although a fallback follows its switch.
classifyOrchestratorThrow documentation incorrectly calls an exported helper module-private.
The remaining reviewed production and test files are clean.
Compiler-forced exhaustive branches are appropriate structural evidence.
Current sibling tests demonstrate strong whole-value notification assertions.
Background reconcile helpers are outside this review's scope.
The historical review did not run tests or coverage.
The review covers notify, backfill, pending, types, and reconcile messaging pairs.
The suites use clear structure and exact whole-value assertions.
Filesystem suites use hermetic temporary roots.
Notification-boundary doubles assert exact ordered calls and offline behavior.
Renderer tests prove tri-state severity and grammar.
reasonAsContent lacked direct sentinel coverage in the historical review.
Scope-qualified structural sentinel reasons have no current producer.
The backfill unavailable branch lacks focused discriminating proof.
The backfill invalid-entry guard is unreachable after validation.
Backfill and pending duplicate a hermetic setup helper.
Pending tests are otherwise clean.
types.test.ts uses a generic subject variable name.
Hybrid runtime and compile-time type tests are appropriate.
Wide compile-only option mocks require an ownership decision.
Reconcile messaging tests are clean.
notify.ts uses terse single-letter callback parameter names.
backfill.ts uses an inline import type.
scanForceInstalledBackfills is exported only for tests.
The reviewed production modules otherwise avoid hidden environmental dependencies.
Current boundary tests provide strong whole-value, ordering, isolation, and readonly reference patterns.
Loose assertion-alias concerns are not supported by the current tests.
The historical review did not run tests or coverage.
